Tourism Strategy
Activities 2020

Name Vortragende

 Marketing Objectives
1.

To be World No1/best known Spa organisation by 2025 (5 year horizon).

2.

To promote sustainable tourism

3.

To generate more visitors based on key performance indicators (KPSs) including:
a.

Length of stay/quality/spend –not just day trippers

b.

Motivation mix – Health/wellbeing/culture/heritage/nature

c.

Younger/Young at heart – tackling the ‘Spas are for old’

d.

Wellbeing/medical – interest at some level

4.

To facilitate reinvention, refresh and rejuvenate the Spa product and associated
infrastructure investment as a physical experience across our 11 cities by 2025

5.

To develop and strengthen the symbiotic relationship between Tourism and
Heritage.

6.

To develop a relationship with residents and stakeholders in our cities to ensure
the retention of goodwill.

 Organisation Plan

What will happen if Great Spas of Europe commit to a more intensive
cooperation in terms of financial and human resources?
Current structure has to be evaluated in legal and organizational
matters.
It could be a difficult task to define an efficient marketing organizational
structure for international cooperation with 11 cities from 7 nations.
Activities:
 to develop optional variants of organizational structures
 to design communication processes  efficient marketing structures

 Brand Development Plan

The brand elaboration of the Great Spas of Europe in December 2017
was a necessary step to show the values and emotions behind the
Great Spas of Europe and to express these in a subsequent Coperate
Design development. Due to the time pressure for the production of
the nomination documents, this brand development was carried out in
only a limited variant.

Activities:
 to write a brand story (create heroes)
 to develop the brand manual
 to adapt the coporate design manual
 to train and promote brand usage

 Communication Plan
To develop a coherent marketing communications plan, based on a strong GSE
Brand and on the authenticity/quality of the Great Spas offering respectively.
Phase 1:

Soft Launch

• Marketing Support to the Nomination
• Basics (Website, Brochure, …

Phase 2:

Crossmarketing

• Crossmarketing activities cities to cities
• GSoE in all indvidual tourism brochures, websites
• Common tourism brochure and actvities

Full
Marketing
Activities:
 Communication Plan 2020
 Commitment on Crossmarketing

• Marketing Strategy
• Annual Communication Plan

 Marketing Budget
Why should any individual GSoE invest in a common marketing budget?
 Great Spas of Europe is a very strong brand, probably even stronger
than any individual city brand.
 There are some possibilities to cooperate and advertise together with
small budgets but to position the Great Spas of Europe as Number 1
Spa organisation all over the world is another story.
 Opportunities to pick up money from ETC or other European
organisations for marketing campaigns.
 If some cities pay towards marketing and others dont could be very
divisive and danger we appear divided to UNESCO.

 Marketing Budget
Layer 1: using the budgeted €16,500money to build a web site and social
media marketing platform to promote the GSE concept and offering.
Layer 2: facilitate a coordination of the existing city marketing through
collaboration to be consistent and begin to cross promote. This would
simply involve funds each city is already spending.
Layer 3: offer the possibility for some cities to pool additional money as
a choice to buy into a particular GSE Marketing campaign
Layer 4: donations by cities in cash or kind towards special projects they
lead or work on with other cities with the help of the GSE – the results of
which would be shared, for example healing health benefits of spa water
research.
Layer 5: Grants from EU – Horizon 2020 (Tourism Strategy) – in
partnership with EHTTA
